thread:
maria: quick heads-up — after last night's runtime deploy p99 for short-chat workloads jumped from 120ms -> ~260ms. Noticed it mostly on kvmiss + small prompt length (<64).
kevin: ugh. do we have a repro? loadtest or prod trace?
jena: i grabbed a perf trace from the canary lane: https://perf/trace/22456 (internal) — looks like kernel switch + repeated kv-warmup on microbatch boundaries.
maria: exact. trace shows frequent kernel flips: attention kernel A -> B based on batch window, happens mid-request when a queued microbatch arrives. p95 unaffected, p99 tails.
samir: can you paste the flame?
maria: ```
# simplified
time   op
0-5ms kv-lookup (miss)
5-18ms kernel-A (small seq)
18-35ms kernel-switch overhead
35-60ms kernel-B (longer seq)
```
kevin: kernel-switch overhead of ~17ms is real. If we choose single kernel by heuristic earlier it helps but reduces throughput for longer sequences. tradeoff.
jena: also saw KV-cache prefetch churn: prefetch thrashes on microbatch boundary so misses spike. That increases total work and pushes util -> saturation -> queueing on GPU.
maria: hypothesis: our microbatch sizing + aggressive util target (90%) causes acceptance of bursty requests and forces kernel-hopping. If we lower headroom or make admission softer we might reduce tail.
ol: perf-bot: loadtest 22456789 completed — 1M requests, avg util 88%, p99 260ms, p95 130ms — baseline (old) p99 115ms.
kevin: thoughts: option A) force kernel selection at request start based on estimated seq length and lock for the request; option B) prefer lower util headroom target (75-80%) for small-req lanes; option C) tune microbatcher delay to avoid mid-request batching that flips kernels.
samir: option A reduces kernel flexibility but removes the mid-request flip cost. We already have per-request metadata (seq_hint). Could be quick patch to prefer single kernel. Risk: throughput drop when guesses wrong.
jena: option C seems low-risk: increase microbatch window by 1-2ms for small seq lanes to avoid capturing trailing tokens that push a batch into a different kernel. Might help p99 with tiny throughput cost.
maria: i ran a quick local sim: increasing microbatch window from 2ms -> 4ms reduced kernel-switch events by 68% and p99 sim reduced by ~45ms. throughput drop ~2%.
kevin: good. also think about soft admission: when GPU util > target && incoming req is small (priority=interactive) accept but set it to lightweight kernel path and avoid prefetch heavy ops.
jena: can we special-case kv-prefetch for these interactive requests? maybe no prefetch on <64 tokens, instead lazy fetch during generation to avoid thrash.
samir: would that increase token latency? maybe slightly but keeps p99 down because no big prefetch spike.
maria: action items: 1) kevin to patch microbatch window toggle for small-req lane (canary next 2 hours). 2) jena to prototype single-kernel-lock heuristic for seq_hint path (bench tomorrow). 3) samir to add metric for kernel-switch count + kv-prefetch spike per minute. 4) ops to lower headroom target for canary fleet to 78% and run soak.
kevin: +1. canary will include the microbatch change and a quick perf trace hook. rolling to canary now.
jena: logged follow-up issue: GH#4321 (kernel-lock experiment)
maria: thanks. if canary shows p99 drop to <160ms we keep. if throughput loss >5% we iterate. ping me in #oncall if any SLO alerts. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: alert suppressed by canary flag.
oliver: FYI i also added a short-load test that spikes kv-miss rate to validate. link: https://ci/2245-kvspike
kevin: rolling patch ID 0a9f -> canary nodes. will post results in ~30m.
maria: perfect — we'll review results and decide whether to push to prod lane. thanks all!
